scope: Theorem 5.7 (Absolute isolated-zero finiteness) of the manuscript “Uniform bounds for planar polynomial limit cycles” (preprints/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026/uniform-bounds-for-planar-polynomial-limit-cycles-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 143 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8ff8e55372a94e4f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 65-66. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let a finite real equation system be specified on an open domain with its original strict inequalities and graph ties. Regard all coordinates, including coefficient parameters and auxiliary coordinates, as variables. Suppose every sequence of distinct solutions has a subsequence with one of the following descriptions: 1. the equations extend as ordinary real analytic functions to a neighborhood of its finite limit; or 2. after finitely many regular graph constructions and coordinate charts, it is an anchored saturated flag regime for a library retestable in the sense of Definition 5.6, with at least one old free 65 input recoverable from the original solution tuple. In the second description every equation admits the finite normalizations and positive operations of Theorem 4.4. Then the system has finitely many isolated real solutions in its full domain. The assertion applies separately to every finite system in the following closure whenever these same sequential hypotheses hold: independent derivatives of equations and domain margins; finite sums, products and regular analytic evaluations; inverses on their specified nonzero domains; denom- inator clearing with those domains retained; fixed real specializations; addition of real parameters, multiplier variables, polynomial equations, and regular graph ties, including finite derivative graphs. No uniform bound over infinitely many generated systems, and no assertion after forgetting their original domains, is part of this theorem.
